description: Refactor build system to decouple data generation from compilation, then augment the public API with query builder, fuzzy search, proper errors, and batch lookups for FFI readiness

userStories.title: Create Cargo workspace with xtask member
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the repo structured as a Cargo workspace with jmdict-fast and xtask as members, so that data generation tooling lives alongside the library.
acceptanceCriteria: Root Cargo.toml defines a workspace with members: jmdict-fast, xtask
xtask/Cargo.toml exists with dependencies: reqwest (blocking, rustls-tls), flate2, tar, serde, serde_json, serde_derive, simd-json, fst, postcard, deunicode, unicode-normalization, anyhow, clap
xtask/src/main.rs has a skeleton main() that parses a 'generate' subcommand using clap and prints 'not yet implemented'
cargo check --workspace succeeds
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move download and caching logic to xtask
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want all JMdict download and caching logic moved from build_utils/ into the xtask crate, so the library has no network dependencies at build time.
acceptanceCriteria: build_utils/cache.rs, build_utils/download.rs, build_utils/dict.rs, and build_utils/mod.rs content is moved to xtask/src/ modules
xtask 'generate' subcommand downloads JMdict simplified JSON using the moved caching logic
jmdict-fast/Cargo.toml no longer has reqwest, flate2, or tar as build-dependencies
build_utils/ directory is removed from jmdict-fast
cargo check --workspace succeeds
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move FST and entries.bin generation to xtask
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the xtask generate command to produce kana.fst, kanji.fst, romaji.fst, id.fst, and entries.bin in a configurable output directory.
acceptanceCriteria: xtask 'generate' subcommand parses downloaded JSON into entries, builds 4 FST maps and serializes entries with postcard
Output files are written to a configurable directory (--output flag, default: dist/)
FST keys are sorted and deduplicated before building
Generation logic from jmdict-fast/build.rs is moved into xtask; build.rs is reduced to only handle include_bytes for embedded mode
Running 'cargo xtask generate' produces valid kana.fst, kanji.fst, romaji.fst, id.fst, entries.bin in dist/
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add binary format version header to entries.bin
userStories.description: As a developer, I want entries.bin to include a magic number and version so that loading mismatched data gives a clear error.
acceptanceCriteria: entries.bin starts with magic bytes b'JMDF' (4 bytes) followed by u32 format version (4 bytes), then entry count and data
Xtask generate writes the magic number and version 1 into generated entries.bin
Dict loading validates magic number and version on open
Mismatched version returns error: 'Data format version X, library expects Y. Regenerate with cargo xtask generate.'
A constant FORMAT_VERSION is defined in jmdict-fast/src/lib.rs
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Feature-gate embedded mode with include_bytes
userStories.description: As a Rust developer, I want an 'embedded' Cargo feature flag that controls whether dictionary data is baked into the binary via include_bytes.
acceptanceCriteria: Cargo.toml defines features = { embedded = [] } with no default features
Dict::load_embedded() is gated behind #[cfg(feature = "embedded")] and uses include_bytes!() for all data files
Without 'embedded' feature, the library builds with no data files on disk
Dict::load_default() tries embedded (if feature enabled), then filesystem path, then JMDICT_DATA env var
build.rs only runs include_bytes logic when 'embedded' feature is active; emits cargo:warning if data files missing
Without 'embedded' feature, build.rs is a no-op
Typecheck passes with: cargo check -p jmdict-fast AND cargo check -p jmdict-fast --features embedded (when dist/ files exist)

userStories.title: Preserve full JMdict entry data
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all JMdict fields preserved in entries.bin so I can access antonyms, dialect info, field tags, and other metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: SenseEntry struct includes all fields: antonym, field, dialect, misc, info, language_source, related (as Vec<String> or Vec<serde_json::Value> as appropriate)
Xtask generate no longer strips these fields during entry processing
Format version is bumped to 2
Existing lookup tests still pass after regenerating data
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: GitHub Actions workflow for release artifacts
userStories.description: As a user of the library, I want pre-built data files attached to GitHub Releases so I can download them without running the xtask.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub Actions workflow runs cargo xtask generate on tagged releases
Bundles kana.fst, kanji.fst, romaji.fst, id.fst, entries.bin into jmdict-data.tar.gz
Attaches jmdict-data.tar.gz to the GitHub Release
Workflow file is at .github/workflows/release.yml
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Update README for new build system and usage
userStories.description: As a new user, I want clear documentation on how to get started with jmdict-fast using either embedded or runtime-loaded modes.
acceptanceCriteria: README covers quick start for both embedded and runtime modes with code examples
Documents cargo xtask generate usage
Documents one-liner download of pre-built data from GitHub Releases
Documents JMDICT_DATA env var and feature flags
Includes migration notes from the previous embedded-only API
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Create JmdictError enum replacing anyhow
userStories.description: As an FFI consumer, I want typed errors with numeric codes so I can handle failures programmatically across the FFI boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: New JmdictError enum in jmdict-fast/src/lib.rs (or src/error.rs)
Variants: DataNotFound, DataVersionMismatch { expected: u32, found: u32 }, DataCorrupted, InvalidQuery, IoError(std::io::Error), DeserializationError
Each variant has a stable numeric code via .code() -> u32 method
impl std::fmt::Display with human-readable messages
impl std::error::Error for JmdictError
All public methods updated to return Result<T, JmdictError> instead of anyhow::Result
anyhow is removed from jmdict-fast runtime dependencies (can remain in xtask)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add LookupResult and MatchType types
userStories.description: As a developer, I want lookup methods to return structured results with metadata so I know how each result matched.
acceptanceCriteria: New LookupResult struct: entry (Entry), match_type (MatchType), match_key (String), score (f64), deinflection (Option<DeinflectionInfo>)
MatchType enum: Exact, Prefix, Deinflected, Fuzzy
DeinflectionInfo struct: original_form (String), base_form (String), rules (Vec<String>)
Existing lookup_exact, lookup_partial, lookup_exact_with_deinflection return Vec<LookupResult> instead of Vec<Entry>
Results sorted by score descending (exact > prefix > deinflected)
All existing tests updated to work with new return type
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement QueryBuilder with mode and execute
userStories.description: As a developer, I want dict.lookup(term) to return a QueryBuilder so I can chain mode selection and execute the query.
acceptanceCriteria: dict.lookup(term) returns a QueryBuilder struct
QueryBuilder has .mode(MatchMode) method; MatchMode enum: Exact, Prefix, Deinflect, Fuzzy
Default mode is Exact
QueryBuilder has .execute() -> Result<Vec<LookupResult>, JmdictError>
Existing convenience methods (lookup_exact, lookup_partial, lookup_exact_with_deinflection) reimplemented using the builder internally
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add filtering to QueryBuilder
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to filter lookup results by commonality and part of speech via the query builder.
acceptanceCriteria: .common_only(bool) filters to entries where any KanjiEntry or KanaEntry has common: true
.pos(&[&str]) filters to entries with matching part_of_speech values in any SenseEntry
.limit(usize) caps results after filtering and sorting
Chaining works: dict.lookup(term).mode(Prefix).common_only(true).pos(&["verb"]).limit(10).execute()?
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement fuzzy search via Levenshtein automaton
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to search with approximate matches using edit distance so misspelled terms still return results.
acceptanceCriteria: MatchMode::Fuzzy triggers Levenshtein automaton search over all FSTs using fst::automaton::Levenshtein
.max_distance(n: u32) on QueryBuilder controls fuzzy tolerance (default: 2)
Fuzzy results have lower scores than exact matches
dict.lookup(term).mode(Fuzzy).max_distance(1).execute()? returns approximate matches
Performance: fuzzy lookup completes in under 50ms for common queries
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add batch lookup API
userStories.description: As an FFI consumer, I want to look up multiple terms in a single call to minimize FFI crossing overhead.
acceptanceCriteria: dict.lookup_batch(&["猫", "犬", "食べる"]) returns a BatchQueryBuilder
BatchQueryBuilder supports same filter methods as QueryBuilder (.common_only, .pos, .limit, .mode)
.execute() returns Vec<(String, Vec<LookupResult>)> — each input term paired with its results
Performance is at least as fast as N individual lookups (shared Dict reference, no repeated setup)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add dictionary metadata API
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to query dictionary metadata so I can display version info and diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: dict.entry_count() -> usize returns total number of entries
dict.version() -> DataVersion returns format version and JMdict source version
DataVersion struct: format_version (u32), jmdict_version (String), generated_at (String)
Version info read from entries.bin header without deserializing entries
Xtask writes JMdict source version and generation timestamp into the header
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add iterator-based results for large result sets
userStories.description: As a developer, I want prefix/fuzzy lookups to return an iterator so large result sets don't allocate unnecessarily.
acceptanceCriteria: QueryBuilder has .execute_iter() returning impl Iterator<Item = LookupResult>
Iterator lazily deserializes entries as consumed
.execute() still exists and collects into Vec
Memory usage for prefix query with 1000+ matches is proportional to consumed results, not total matches
